content.text:
Confirmed. The buggy line was introduced in this commit, which added the `TimedRunnable` class with `taskPendingStats.registerSuccessfulEvent(initNanos, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS)` — passing the absolute timestamp `initNanos` directly instead of computing the elapsed time since `initNanos`. This exact bug was later fixed in 2c001a55 by wrapping it with `MathUtils.elapsedNanos(initNanos)`.

Let me double check this is the only location/commit, and that no other commit touched this specific line in between (to rule out a later reintroduction).

content.text:
This confirms the line was introduced exactly once in `21ceb4c9` and never modified until the fix in `2c001a55`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 21ceb4c958fd3ea71de6229e878c5560c9f94385

## Reasoning
(1) The fixing commit's most semantically meaningful change (as opposed to the test/stats-plumbing additions) is in `OrderedScheduler.java` (formerly `OrderedSafeExecutor.java`): `taskPendingStats.registerSuccessfulEvent(initNanos, ...)` was changed to use `MathUtils.elapsedNanos(initNanos)`. I used `git log --follow -p` on that file to trace every revision of this exact line across renames.

(2) The history shows the line `taskPendingStats.registerSuccessfulEvent(initNanos, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);` was introduced in commit `21ceb4c958fd3ea71de6229e878c5560c9f94385`, as part of adding the `TimedRunnable` wrapper class (which records how long a task waited in queue before running, and how long it took to execute). `initNanos` is set in the constructor via `MathUtils.nowInNano()` — i.e., it is an absolute timestamp captured when the task was submitted, not an elapsed duration. Passing this raw timestamp directly to `registerSuccessfulEvent` means the "pending time" stat recorded nanosecond-epoch-like absolute values instead of the actual queueing latency — a correctness bug in stats reporting (the values would be enormous/meaningless rather than a small elapsed duration).

(3) Evidence: `git log --follow -p` on the file shows this line was added in `21ceb4c9` (Oct 2015) and remained completely unchanged through all subsequent commits in the file's history until `2c001a55` (the supplied fix), which is the only commit that modifies it — wrapping `initNanos` in `MathUtils.elapsedNanos(...)` to correctly compute elapsed time from the captured timestamp to "now." No other intervening commit touched this line, so `21ceb4c9` is the sole introducer of the bug.

I'm highly confident in this attribution — the line in question has a single, unambiguous origin commit, and the nature of the change in the fix (wrapping an absolute timestamp with an elapsed-time computation) directly matches a missing step in the original addition.
